requirements.title: Settings opens as a single reused, non-resizable 780 x 580 AppKit window titled "Settings"
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:21 Size.settings - NSSize(width: 780, height: 580)

DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:80-84 makeSettingsWindow() - makeWindow(title: "Settings", size: Size.settings, resizable: false, windowClass: SecondaryWindow.self) { SettingsView() }; window.center()
DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:32-37 showSettings(page:) - `let window = settingsWindow ?? makeSettingsWindow(); settingsWindow = window`, so one window is built once and reused

DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:92-99 makeWindow - style [.titled, .closable, .miniaturizable, .fullSizeContentView]; resizable is NOT inserted for settings; window.title = title; window.isReleasedWhenClosed = false; window.animationBehavior = .documentWindow; window.tabbingMode = .disallowed; WindowChrome.configure(window)
requirements.preconditions: The application is running. The settings window may or may not already exist.
requirements.action: Anything calls WindowManager.shared.showSettings(page:) - the Settings shortcut, a menu item, or an in-app link.
requirements.expected_result: The settings window is created the first time and reused on every later call. Its title is the literal "Settings". Its content size is 780 x 580 points. It has a close button and a minimise button and a full-size content view, and it is NOT resizable (the .resizable style mask bit is only inserted when `resizable` is true, and settings passes false). Window tabbing is disallowed. Closing the window does not release it, so its state survives a close and reopen.
side_effects: Creates one NSWindow and one hosted SwiftUI view tree on first open
requirements.persistence: The settings window has no frame autosave name (unlike the main window's "DroppyCodeMainWindow"), so its position is not persisted across launches.
failure_cases: None. The window is created unconditionally.
requirements.windows_path: A separate BrowserWindow (or equivalent modal-less child window) of exactly 780 x 580 client area, resizable: false, minimizable: true, with the same title. Windows has no window tabbing, so tabbingMode has no analogue and is dropped. isReleasedWhenClosed maps to hiding rather than destroying the window on close so its in-memory state survives. There is no menu bar (OD-0008 C3): the window opens from the Settings shortcut (Ctrl+, by default, OD-0008 B7), the command palette and the in-app links, never from a menu item. ED-063 (probe P7, porting/probes/p7/RESULT.md): on Avalonia 12.1.2 app-drawn caption controls declared only through Win32Properties.SetNonClientHitTestResult do nothing and right-click opens no system menu, so the window keeps WindowDecorations.Full with ExtendClientAreaToDecorationsHint, declares its leading-edge controls and drag region through SetNonClientHitTestResult, and a WndProc hook performs the controls' actions (WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN on a control swallowed, the SC_* command posted on WM_NCLBUTTONUP) and shows the system menu on WM_CONTEXTMENU and SC_KEYMENU. ED-063 records this for the main window; the settings window's caption controls are configured by the same WindowChrome.configure (WindowManager.swift:101), so the same hook serves them.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: open settings, assert window size and title; close and reopen, assert the same window instance state (selected page) is retained

deviation.upstream: The Settings item of the macOS app menu opens the window (App/AppCommands.swift:12-14 `CommandGroup(replacing: .appSettings) { Button("Settings…") { WindowManager.shared.showSettings() }`).
deviation.port: No menu bar. Every command the source defines stays on its shortcut and in the command palette; text fields keep standard Ctrl+C/V/X/Z/A

requirements.title: Opening settings centres the window over the main window and clamps it onto that screen
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:32-37 showSettings(page:) - calls centerOverMainWindow(window) then present(window)

DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:40-55 centerOverMainWindow(_:) - guard main window exists, isVisible and not miniaturized else window.center(); origin.x = (parent.midX - frame.width / 2).rounded(); origin.y = (parent.midY - frame.height / 2).rounded(); then clamped into (main.screen ?? NSScreen.main)?.visibleFrame with min/max on both axes; window.setFrame(frame, display: false)
DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:57-60 present(_:) - NSApp.activate(); window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
requirements.preconditions: Settings is being shown.
requirements.action: showSettings runs.
requirements.expected_result: If the main window exists, is visible and is not minimised, the settings window is moved so its centre is on the main window's centre, with both coordinates rounded to whole points, then clamped so its left edge is at least the screen's visible minX and its right edge at most visible maxX, and likewise vertically. If the main window is missing, hidden or minimised, the window is centred on screen instead. The frame is set with display: false. Then the application is activated and the window is made key and ordered front.
side_effects: Activates the application
failure_cases: No screen available: the visibleFrame clamp is skipped (the optional chain yields nil) and the centred frame is used unclamped.
requirements.windows_path: Compute the centred rectangle against the main window's bounds and clamp into the work area of the display the main window is on (Electron screen.getDisplayMatching), then show and focus.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a main window at a known position on a known display

requirements.preconditions: The Shortcuts page is showing.
requirements.action: The user records, clears or resets a shortcut.
requirements.expected_result: A dictionary keyed by the shortcut's raw value, holding an Override whose chord is either the new chord or nil. Recording a chord equal to the shipped default removes the override entirely rather than storing it, so the store only ever names genuinely customised commands. Clearing a shortcut stores an override whose chord is nil, which is what distinguishes 'cleared' from 'default'. The whole dictionary is re-encoded and written on every change. It is written to the standard defaults suite directly, not through the settings store's suite.
side_effects: One defaults write per change
failure_cases: Stored data that fails to decode: the store starts empty, so every shortcut falls back to its default, and the next change overwrites the blob.
requirements.windows_path: The stored contents cannot be carried over: keyCode values are macOS virtual key codes and modifiers are raw NSEvent.ModifierFlags bits. The port defines its own chord format over Windows virtual-key codes and starts from defaults; this is a recorded, deliberate incompatibility, not a translation. Keep the same key name, the same 'absent means default, present-with-null means cleared' three-state model, and the same 'equal to default removes the override' rule.
requirements.verification_method: unit test over the three states; restart test; explicit test that a macOS blob is discarded rather than misread

requirements.preconditions: The About page is showing or the background checker has run.
requirements.action: A check completes, or the app launches.

All three live in the standard defaults suite, deliberately not in the settings store that a capture profile redirects, so the About page can show a known update the instant it opens. requirements.windows_path: Same three key names in the port's own store slice, kept out of any profile-redirected settings file. requirements.action: The user presses the grip and drags.
requirements.expected_result: The grip is a "line.3.horizontal" glyph that brightens from 70% to full opacity on hover, with the tooltip and accessibility label the verbatim "Drag to reorder". It shows the grab-idle pointer style whenever this row is not the one being dragged, and the grab-active pointer style while it is; SwiftUI applies and clears this cursor for the grip's own hit area, so there is no push/pop pair to balance. A drag begins after 1 point of movement, measured in global coordinates. The grabbed row follows the pointer with animations explicitly disabled for the offset, so it tracks exactly. On every move the visible order is read fresh, not captured at the start, and the row swaps past every visible neighbour whose centre it has crossed, using each neighbour's measured height including its divider, falling back to 54 points for a row that has not reported a height yet; the neighbours slide with a spring of response 0.28 and damping 0.82. Each swap that actually changes the list fires an alignment haptic. While a search filters the list, swaps still happen against the visible neighbour, so hidden models keep their place relative to it. Releasing settles the row with a spring of response 0.32 and damping 0.8; the grip's pointer style falls back to grab-idle because isDragged becomes false.

requirements.cancellation: Releasing ends the drag; there is no cancel that restores the original order.

requirements.preconditions: The Shortcuts page is showing.
requirements.action: The user reads or re-records the "New thread" row.
requirements.expected_result: A row in the "Threads" card whose left side is the verbatim title "New thread" on one line, truncated at the tail, with the verbatim sentence "Starts a thread in the current project." as its tooltip rather than as a visible second line. Its recorder shows Ctrl+N while the shortcut is at its default or has been re-recorded to a chord, and the words "Record shortcut" once it has been cleared. The shipped chord renders as Ctrl+N; upstream it is ⌘N, stored as key code 45 with modifiers .command. The persisted override key is the raw value "newThread".
requirements.persistence: An override is stored under the key "newThread" inside the "keyboardShortcuts" JSON blob; a chord equal to Ctrl+N removes the override instead of storing it.
failure_cases: A recorded chord that another command already owns is refused with that command's title; see the refusal requirement.
The shortcut is cleared: the recorder reads "Record shortcut" and the command has no key.
requirements.cancellation: Escape with no modifiers held cancels the recording without changing anything.
requirements.windows_path: The command and its title and tooltip carry over verbatim. The chord does NOT: key code 45 is a macOS virtual key code and the modifier bits are AppKit's, so the port defines the equivalent chord over Windows virtual-key codes and its own modifier set. The Command modifier maps to Control on Windows, which is the default the port ships; port_impacts.md:228 entry 110 requires the persisted blob to be re-defined and the defaults re-derived rather than migrated. Chords render in Windows notation (OD-0008 B7): modifiers as Ctrl, Alt and Shift joined with "+" before the key label, with the ED-050 mapping Command->Ctrl, Option->Alt, Shift->Shift, Control->Ctrl; key labels keep upstream's US-position table (OD-0008 B9). This shortcut therefore reads Ctrl+N.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the shortcut table asserting the title, tooltip, raw value, section and default chord; interaction test recording and resetting the row

deviation.upstream: The recorder and every hint render the shipped chord as the glyph string ⌘N (KeyChord.description, Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:32-34, with the modifier glyphs of :43-50 concatenated with no separator).

DroppyCode/App/AppCommands.swift:57-58 at 1fbf81e6 - `Button("Actual Size") { model.settings.appZoom = 100 }` `.keyboardShortcut("0", modifiers: .command)`, a hard-coded chord equal to this command's default (key code 29 is the 0 position), outside the shortcut store
porting/owner_decisions.md OD-0002 - "Every user-visible occurrence of the product name inside the app becomes a rename point"; the Windows build ships as Marrow
requirements.preconditions: The Shortcuts page is showing.
requirements.action: The user reads or re-records the "Show Droppy Code" row.
requirements.expected_result: A row in the "Window and panels" card whose left side is the title "Show Marrow" (upstream the verbatim "Show Droppy Code"; its product name is the OD-0002 rename point) on one line, truncated at the tail, with the verbatim sentence "Brings the main window to the front." as its tooltip rather than as a visible second line. In Marrow the command ships with no default chord (OD-0012 G6), so its recorder shows the words "Record shortcut" at its default and after it has been cleared, and the recorded chord in Windows notation once one has been recorded; upstream it ships with ⌘0, stored as key code 29 with modifiers .command. The persisted override key is the raw value "showMainWindow". Ctrl+0 is the hard-coded "Actual Size" zoom command added at 1fbf81e6 (AppCommands.swift:57-58). Upstream both answer Command-0 while this command keeps its default; OD-0012 G6 settles that overlap for the default by giving this command none.
requirements.persistence: An override is stored under the key "showMainWindow" inside the "keyboardShortcuts" JSON blob. Because the default is no chord (OD-0012 G6), clearing the shortcut equals the default and removes the override instead of storing it, and any recorded chord is stored (Shortcuts.swift:300-301 `overrides[shortcut.rawValue] = chord == shortcut.defaultChord ? nil : Override(chord: chord)`, with defaultChord optional at :214).
failure_cases: A recorded chord that another command already owns is refused with that command's title; see the refusal requirement.
The shortcut is cleared: the recorder reads "Record shortcut" and the command has no key.

Upstream, while the default is kept, Command-0 is held both by this command and by the hard-coded "Actual Size" zoom command. In Marrow this command has no default chord (OD-0012 G6), so by default Ctrl+0 is Actual Size alone. A user who records Ctrl+0 for this command recreates the overlap; which of the two then fires is not expressed in source and stays UNRESOLVED with the window area (PR-WIN-224, PR-WIN-226); the port must not pick one silently.
requirements.cancellation: Escape with no modifiers held cancels the recording without changing anything.
requirements.windows_path: The command and its tooltip carry over verbatim; the title carries over except for the product name (OD-0002). The chord does NOT: by owner ruling OD-0012 G6 the command ships with no default chord, because Ctrl+0 is Actual Size and the window can no longer hide (OD-0008 C1). A chord the user records is defined over Windows virtual-key codes and the port's own modifier set (key code 29 is a macOS virtual key code and the modifier bits are AppKit's); port_impacts.md:228 entry 110 requires the persisted blob to be re-defined and the defaults re-derived rather than migrated. The title contains the product name, which the approved rename (OD-0002) changes, so it reads "Show Marrow" (OD-0002; OD-0012 F1); every other title is fixed product text. Chords render in Windows notation (OD-0008 B7): modifiers as Ctrl, Alt and Shift joined with "+" before the key label, with the ED-050 mapping Command->Ctrl, Option->Alt, Shift->Shift, Control->Ctrl; key labels keep upstream's US-position table (OD-0008 B9). This shortcut therefore shows "Record shortcut" until one is recorded. The hard-coded zoom command "Actual Size" keeps Ctrl+0 (PR-WIN-224; OD-0012 G6).
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the shortcut table asserting the title "Show Marrow", tooltip, raw value, section and the absence of a default chord (the recorder reads "Record shortcut"); interaction test recording and resetting the row

It ships with the chord ⌘0 (Core/Models/Shortcuts.swift:233), which the hard-coded "Actual Size" command (App/AppCommands.swift:57-58) also answers.

requirements.title: A recording session swallows every key event, judges a chord the moment its key goes down, and commits 300ms after the last key is released
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:489-490 doc - "One recording, from the click on the control to the popover folding away. A chord is judged the moment its key goes down and can be replaced while anything is held; it saves once every key is up."

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:525-562 begin - closes any running session, resets state, seeds heldModifiers from the currently held modifiers masked to control, option, shift and command, refreshes the caps, marks itself active, installs `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: [.keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged])` which returns nil for every handled event (so the app never sees them) and the event itself only for other types, and observes NSApplication.didResignActiveNotification to cancel

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:583-594 handleFlagsChanged - updates the held modifiers; a newly added modifier performs an alignment haptic; with no modifiers and no key held it lets go, otherwise it refreshes the caps; it does nothing while finishing

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:596-608 handleKeyDown - ignores auto-repeats; `if keyCode == 53, flags.isEmpty { cancel(); return }`; otherwise records the held key and modifiers and judges the chord
DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:610-619 handleKeyUp - only for the held key; clears it; lets go when no modifiers remain, otherwise refreshes the caps

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:621-633 judge - latches the chord; a refusal sets the rejected verdict, shows the refusal message and performs a generic haptic; otherwise it sets the accepted verdict, clears the message and performs a level-change haptic

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:635-657 letGo - with no latched chord it only refreshes; accepted marks itself finishing, refreshes, then after 300 milliseconds commits the chord and closes, provided the task was not cancelled and the session is still active; rejected drops the latched chord and returns to listening; listening only refreshes

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:569-581 close - cancels the finish task, removes the event monitor and the resign observer, clears the active and finishing flags, and calls the close callback exactly once

DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:659-674 refreshCaps - with a latched chord and a verdict, the chord's caps; otherwise the held modifiers as pressed caps, plus the held key's cap when one is down, or a ghost key when not; with no modifiers at all, a single ghost Command cap; the caps are written only when they changed
requirements.preconditions: A recording popover is open.
requirements.action: The user presses and releases a key combination.
requirements.expected_result: Every key down, key up and modifier change is consumed by the session and never reaches the rest of the app. Auto-repeats are ignored. Pressing Escape with no modifiers held cancels the session outright; Escape with a modifier is treated as an ordinary key. Adding a modifier fires an alignment haptic and redraws the caps. Pressing a key judges the chord immediately: accepted fires a level-change haptic and turns the caps green, refused fires a generic haptic, turns them red and shows the refusal message. While anything is still held the chord can be replaced by pressing a different key. When the last key and modifier are released, an accepted chord is committed 300 milliseconds later and the popover closes; a refused chord is discarded and the session returns to listening with the caps back to neutral. Closing removes the monitor and the observer and calls the close callback once. The application losing focus cancels the session.
side_effects: Blocks all key input to the rest of the app while open
Fires haptics
Writes the shortcut store on commit
failure_cases: A refused chord: it is never committed; the message is shown and recording continues.
The app is sent to the background mid-recording: the session cancels and nothing is committed.
requirements.cancellation: Bare Escape, dismissing the popover, the row disappearing, or the app resigning active. The 300ms commit task is cancelled by all of them.
requirements.windows_path: A window-level capture-phase key listener with preventDefault and stopPropagation on every keydown, keyup and modifier change while the popover is open, plus a blur handler that cancels. port_impacts.md:424 entry 208 records that this is one of five separate Escape policies in the family and must be decided on its own: here bare Escape cancels and Escape with a modifier is recordable. The haptics become a no-op shim; do not substitute a sound or an animation.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test covering accept, refuse, replace-while-held, bare Escape, modified Escape, blur, and the 300ms commit delay

requirements.preconditions: A chord has just been judged.
requirements.action: The store is asked whether the chord can be taken.
requirements.expected_result: The checks run in exactly this order and the first that fires wins. A chord identical to the shortcut's current one is always allowed, so re-recording the same keys is not a conflict with itself. A bare modifier key gives the verbatim "Add a key to the modifiers." A key that types text or moves the caret, pressed with no modifier other than Shift, gives the verbatim "Add Ctrl or Alt so typing still works." (OD-0008 B7; upstream "Add ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ so typing still works."). A key with no menu equivalent gives the verbatim "Menus cannot use this key." One of the reserved chords gives the verbatim "Windows or Marrow already uses this chord." (OD-0008 B8; upstream "macOS or Droppy Code already uses this chord."). A chord another command already holds gives that command's title followed by the verbatim " already uses this chord.", for example "Command palette already uses this chord." The reserved list is the upstream table kept as is (OD-0008 B8) under the ED-050 modifier mapping: Ctrl with Q, H, M, C, V, X, A and Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, and Ctrl with each digit 1 through 9.
requirements.persistence: None; a refused chord is never stored.
failure_cases: The four hard-coded zoom chords (Ctrl with +, -, 0 and =, upstream Command) are neither reserved nor AppShortcut commands. Recording Ctrl+- or Ctrl+= for a command is accepted with no message and then shares its chord with a zoom command; Ctrl+0 is refused only while a command holds it, and then by the owner check naming that command, not "Actual Size"; in Marrow no command holds it by default, because showMainWindow ships with no default chord (OD-0012 G6), so recording Ctrl+0 is accepted with no message and shares the chord with Actual Size. Which command fires on a shared chord is not expressed in source (UNRESOLVED; PR-WIN-226). Reproduce the absence of a guard; do not add the zoom chords to the reserved list.
requirements.windows_path: Keep the five checks in the same ORDER so the same chord produces the same message. Two messages are reworded by owner ruling: "Add Ctrl or Alt so typing still works." (B7) and "Windows or Marrow already uses this chord." (B8); the other three stay verbatim. The reserved table is kept as is (B8), with Command read as Ctrl per ED-050, and must stay in sync with the hard-coded thread-jump chords as one unit (port_impacts.md:228 entry 110).
requirements.verification_method: unit test over one chord per refusal reason plus the self-match case, asserting the exact Windows strings "Add Ctrl or Alt so typing still works." and "Windows or Marrow already uses this chord.", the unchanged three, the 18 reserved chords and the order of precedence

requirements.expected_result: The field is populated from the stored key when the section first appears, and that population does NOT count as an edit: the guard compares the field against the stored value, so no write and no check happen. requirements.preconditions: A release's notes are being parsed.
requirements.action: parse is called.
requirements.expected_result: Nil or empty notes give an empty digest. The same raw text as last time returns the cached digest. Otherwise the text is walked line by line, each line trimmed of spaces: blank lines, a bare "---" and any line starting with "<" are skipped. A line whose first character is one of the seven bullet markers and whose second is a space or a tab is a bullet; it is dropped when no category is current, and otherwise has its links, bold and inline code stripped in that order (each replaced by its captured text, then trimmed of spaces and tabs) and is appended if what remains is non-empty. A heading that matches one of the nine accepted names, case-insensitively and after stripping hashes, bold markers, spaces, tabs and colons, becomes the current category; the accepted names are "new features" and "new"; "bug fixes", "fixes" and "bugs"; "refinements" and "improvements". Any other heading clears the current category, so bullets under a "Thanks to contributors" heading are left out. A heading is a line of one or more hashes followed by nothing, a space or a tab, or a line wrapped in double asterisks longer than four characters; a plain sentence ending in a colon is not a heading. Then, for each of the three categories in declaration order, an empty one is omitted, duplicates are removed case-insensitively keeping the first occurrence, and if the last remaining bullet contains a numeric word immediately before a word that reduces to "extra", that bullet becomes the section's rollup and its number is added to the change count rather than being listed as a change.
requirements.persistence: None; the memo is in-memory and holds only the last parse.
failure_cases: Notes in no recognised shape: the digest is empty and the page shows the raw notes as markdown instead.
requirements.windows_path: Same grammar, the same seven bullet markers, the same nine heading names, the same three strip passes in order and the same rollup rule. Memoise on the raw text for the same reason.

requirements.title: The install progress slider chases a forward-only target every display frame and stops the clock when it catches up
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/AboutUpdateViews.swift:305-337 FractionChase - doc "Per-frame exponential chase of a target that only moves forward, so a download's uneven reports become one continuous glide."; the first advance snaps to the target; a target below the displayed value snaps to it; otherwise the elapsed time is clamped into 0 through 0.25 seconds and the step is the remaining distance times (1 - exp(-dt / max(response, 0.01))), floored at the minimum speed times dt, and the displayed value is capped at the target; within one ten-thousandth of the target it snaps, so the clock can stop

requirements.preconditions: An install is reporting progress, or the post-relaunch sweep is running.
requirements.action: The slider renders.
requirements.expected_result: A pill track 14 points tall with a 20-point head. The displayed fraction chases the reported target once per display frame at up to 60 frames a second, exponentially, never going backwards except by snapping when the target itself drops. The frame clock is paused as soon as the displayed value reaches the target, and while anything in the app is scrolling, and restarts when the target moves. The chase is seeded with the target's current value at mount, so the post-relaunch sweep does not open from zero. The fill is a three-stop blue gradient anchored to the whole track and revealed by a leading clip, fading in between fractions 0.012 and 0.05 on a smoothstep; 14 sparkles twinkle in the filled part from a deterministic field and are suppressed entirely under Reduce Motion. The head is a white circle at 96% opacity whose inner disc is 64% of its frame, travelling between the two end-cap centres. The whole control is one accessibility element labelled the verbatim "Updating Marrow" (OD-0012 F1; upstream "Updating Droppy Code") whose value is the fraction as a whole-number percentage. During the celebration phase the chase uses a slower response of 0.72 with a minimum speed of 0.12 so the sweep is visible; otherwise 0.3 with no floor; Reduce Motion uses 0.15 in both cases.
side_effects: Runs a per-frame timeline while the value is moving
requirements.cancellation: The timeline pauses when settled or while scrolling; the celebration task is cancelled when the page is left.
requirements.windows_path: Same chase maths, the same pause conditions and the same sparkle determinism so a capture comparison is reproducible. Reduce Motion is read live from the system animation setting.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the chase function including the dt clamp and the snap threshold; capture comparison at fractions 0.01, 0.03, 0.5 and 1

requirements.title: A watchdog task started by the first active report polls every 2 seconds and drops timelines whose reporter is gone or resting
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Common/RenderBudget.swift:23 - @ObservationIgnored private var watch: Task<Void, Never>?

DroppyCode/UI/Common/RenderBudget.swift:44-63 - if now, watch == nil { watch = Task { @MainActor [weak self] in while !Task.isCancelled { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2)); guard let self, !Task.isCancelled else { return }; for id in Array(scrolling) { guard let reporter = reporters[id]?.object, reporter.isScrollingNow else { scrolling.remove(id); reporters[id] = nil; continue } }; let still = !scrolling.isEmpty; if still != isScrolling { isScrolling = still }; if !still { watch = nil; return } } } }
requirements.preconditions: At least one timeline has just reported true and no watchdog is running.
requirements.action: Two seconds elapse with the set non-empty.
requirements.expected_result: At most one watchdog exists at a time: it is created only when the flag has just become true AND watch is nil. It sleeps FIRST and checks afterwards, so a stale reporter survives at least one full 2 second period. Each pass iterates a COPY of the id set (Array(scrolling)) so it can mutate the set while iterating; for each id it drops both the id and the reporter entry when the weak reporter has gone OR when the live reporter answers isScrollingNow == false; a reporter that answers true is left alone. After the sweep it recomputes the union and publishes it only on a change. When the set has emptied it clears its own handle (watch = nil) and returns, so the next active report starts a fresh task. The task holds self weakly and returns immediately if self is gone or the task was cancelled.
requirements.windows_path: A single timer or interval, at most one at a time, fixed at 2000 milliseconds, that sleeps before its first check, sweeps over a snapshot of the ids, removes dead or resting reporters, republishes the union and then clears itself when nothing is left. Do not shorten the period or check before the first sleep: a reporter is expected to be briefly registered and resting between a drag and its coast. Note the latent hazard the signature allows: a caller that reports true with no reporter leaves a nil weak entry, and the first sweep then drops that timeline after 2 seconds even though it really is scrolling.
